title: Choose the visual world for the Outbound CRM
question: The roll assigned the Scorecard & DRS world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Scorecard & DRS
options.lineage: printed cricket scorecards and the Decision Review System broadcast panel
options.thesis: Every account is a batting entry; every agent-loop fix is a decision overturned on review.
options.viewport: Top bar with run box; proof strip of 4 numbers each against its baseline; a DRS panel showing ORIGINAL vs ON REVIEW for overturned calls beside a fall-of-wickets funnel; the scorecard table below.
options.risk: Cricket fluency helps; the panels must still read to someone who has never watched a match.

raised.raise: A changed row stays lit until the Growth Lead opens it.
Columns never move between runs; only their values update in place.
One chart owns each panel; nothing else competes in it.
A strict 1px hairline grid aligns every panel edge.
A five-step type scale; hierarchy by weight and colour, not size jumps.
Every account carries the same fixed furniture: score, how-out, contact, email score.

options.label: Auditor's Workpaper
options.lineage: audit workpapers with tick-mark legends and W/P cross-references
options.thesis: Every number carries an auditor's tick mark that says how it was verified.
options.viewport: Top bar; a tick-mark legend strip; proof numbers each with its tick mark; accounts table where every cell links to its source.
options.risk: The most expected direction for a compliance product; sober to the point of dry.

options.label: Gate Board & Boarding Pass
options.lineage: airport departure boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: Accounts rank like departures; a changed status reflows in place and stays lit.
options.viewport: A ranked board of accounts by next action, with the selected account as a segmented pass on the right.
options.case: Holds product clarity (a ranking you watch); loses audience identification to cricket.
options.risk: Travel framing says nothing about evidence or compliance.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Accounts as departures on a flap board.
options.risk: A costume of a display instrument on a working screen.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to sales or evidence.
options.kept: Columns never move; only values change.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.thesis: The CRM as a tabbed reference manual.
options.viewport: Stepped tab rail beside one leaf.
options.risk: Reads as documentation, not a live tool.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.risk: Coding names as colour strips fights self-explanation.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Accounts as plates in an annual.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Accounts as a ranked mascot roster.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS sales dashboard (Attio, Linear Insights), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: KPI row, funnel chart and a sortable accounts table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dashboard by design.
